results.term_definition: The solar constant is the average amount of electromagnetic radiation (light energy) from the Sun that is received per unit time per unit area (oriented normal to the Sun's direction) at the distance of one astronomical unit (the average distance from the Earth to the Sun). It is currently equal to about 1361 watts per square meter in vacuum (outside the Earth's atmosphere). While not a physical constant, it varies by less than 0.2% over hundreds of years. However, because Earth's orbit is elliptical the flux density at the distance of Earth varies by 7%. As the Sun evolves it is slowly getting brighter, so over billions of years this value will increase significantly.
